# marked, with a photo
Edit the first attached picture: it is part of a black-and-white photo that is 3D printed as a lithophane, a panel in white PLA that is thicker where the photo is dark and thinner where it is bright, so it shows the photo when lit from behind, so only its grey tones show: a full range of tones from deep shadow to bright highlight, with no flat or washed-out areas. The second attached picture is the same part with the area to change outlined in magenta; the third is the whole photo, for context only.
Change only this inside the outlined area: swap the man on the left for the man in the photo
The attached photo shows the real person or subject for the part you change: keep their likeness.
Keep everything else exactly as it is: the same picture size and framing, and every person, object, edge and tone outside the outlined area where it is; copy them, don't redraw them. Answer with the first picture changed, without the magenta outline.
Rules for what you change:
- a realistic photo, like the rest of the picture: the same light, focus, grain, brightness and contrast, so that it blends in with no visible seam
- a full tonal range in the change too (real shadows and highlights, not flat grey): the lit panel shows the tones
- in grey tones only, as the rest of the picture (the print has no colour)
- no outline, border or frame around the change, and no text, signature or watermark
